Education / Coaching & test-prep institutes

From demo class to results day, with honest claims and attentive mentors

Coaching and test-prep institutes win students in short, intense seasons and keep them through months of tests and doubts. We automate demo-to-enrollment follow-up, batch schedules, attendance alerts to parents, test analytics and doubt routing, designed around the Ministry of Education coaching guidelines and the consumer authority's advertising rules.

The challenge

What makes coaching & test-prep institutes different.

01

Seminar and ad leads pile up on counselors' phones, demo attendees are not followed up, and each counselor explains fees and refunds differently.

02

Batch changes, faculty absences and extra classes are announced in large groups that students mute, so classes and tests are missed.

03

Mock test results show marks and ranks but not why a student is struggling, and doubts sent by photo wait days or reach the wrong faculty.

04

Advertising and results claims face consumer authority scrutiny, and state coaching laws add registration, refund and student well-being duties.

Where automation helps

Practical uses for coaching & test-prep institutes.

01

Demo class to enrollment

Demo slots booked from ads and seminars, attendance recorded, a counselor call with demo feedback, and the fee plan and refund policy sent in writing before any payment.

02

Batch allocation and change notices

Students placed by course, medium, center and timing within capacity, and every schedule change sent only to the affected batch and, for minors, their parents.

03

Attendance alerts to parents

Absence from a class or test notifies the parent of a student under eighteen the same day, and repeated absence goes to the student's mentor for a conversation.

04

Faculty absence cover

When a faculty member is absent, the coordinator gets a proposed substitute or reschedule and approves the notice before it reaches the batch.

05

Topic-level test analytics

Each mock test produces a private topic and time analysis against the student's own history, shared with the student and parent, with mentors alerted to sharp drops.

06

Doubt routing to faculty

Doubts sent as photos or text are tagged by subject and chapter and queued to the right faculty, with similar solved questions from your own bank attached.

Visit, demo or trialStarter2–4 weeks

Demo class to enrollment for coaching institutes

Leads from ads, school seminars and walk-ins book a demo class, get reminders and, after attending, a counselor call informed by their demo feedback. The fee plan, installment schedule, refund policy and batch options go out in writing before any payment.

Coaching & test-prep institutes

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Coaching admissions peak around board results and entrance exam calendars. Demo attendees are not followed up consistently, counselors explain fees and refunds differently, and pressure tactics or rank promises in follow-up messages now attract consumer authority action.

Trigger

An aspirant or parent submits an ad or seminar form, walks in, or messages the institute about a course or demo class.

How it runs

  • Record the lead with course, target exam, class, center and source, and check the institute's minimum age and eligibility rules before offering a demo.
  • Offer demo slots by course and center, send an approved confirmation with timing and address, and remind the aspirant and, for minors, the parent before the class.
  • Mark demo attendance from the faculty's register or app, and send a two-question feedback form after the class.
  • Create a counselor task with the feedback and preferred batch timing; the counselor calls to discuss fit and preparation, never rank or selection promises.
  • Send the written fee plan, installment schedule, refund policy and batch options from approved templates, with a payment link only after the family confirms.
  • Report demo bookings, attendance and enrollments by course, center and source, and flag leads waiting more than a day for a call.

Human checkpoint

Counselors hold every enrollment conversation, and the center head approves any discount or installment change. The academic head and the institute's legal adviser approve all templates so that none promises selections, ranks or assured results.

Onboard and scheduleStandard3–5 weeks

Batch and cohort allocation with schedule change notices

New students are placed in batches or live cohorts by course, center or time zone, medium and timing within capacity. Faculty availability is checked, timetables are published, and every later change reaches only the affected students and parents.

Coaching & test-prep institutes · EdTech & online learning

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Batches fill unevenly, timing preferences live in spreadsheets, and schedule changes are announced in large groups that students mute. In coaching, timings may also need to respect school hours and daily limits under state coaching rules or the institute's own policy.

Trigger

A student completes enrollment, a batch reaches capacity, or a coordinator changes a class time, room, faculty member or mode.

How it runs

  • Read enrollments with course, center or time zone, medium and preferred timing, and propose placements within room and faculty capacity.
  • Check proposed timetables against the rules the institute sets, such as no classes during school hours, a weekly off and a maximum daily duration.
  • Show the plan to the academic coordinator, who adjusts and approves placements and timetables.
  • Publish each student's batch, timetable and room or joining link in the app, and confirm it to the student and, for minors, the parent.
  • When a class moves, notify only that batch with a one-tap acknowledgment, and re-send to anyone who has not opened it before the class.

Human checkpoint

The academic coordinator approves every placement, batch transfer and timetable change, and faculty confirm their availability. Requests to move a student between batches are decided by the academic head, never by the scheduler.

Attend and learnStandard3–5 weeks

Absence, late arrival and school bus alerts to parents

Students marked absent without approved leave trigger a private message to the parent by a set time, with reply buttons, and bus boarding, drop and delay updates come from RFID or attendant app events. Unresolved cases reach a staff member who calls the family.

K-12 schools · Coaching & test-prep institutes

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Calling every absent student's family takes a teacher's free period, so calls are late or skipped. Parents of bus students cannot tell whether their child boarded, and the transport office spends the morning answering the same calls.

Trigger

The attendance cutoff passes with a student marked absent and no approved leave, or a bus RFID reader or the attendant's app records a boarding, drop or delay.

How it runs

  • At the cutoff the institution sets, read attendance from the ERP or biometric system and list students absent without approved leave.
  • Send the parent an approved utility template with buttons for known reason, arriving late or did not know, and log the reply against the attendance record.
  • When the parent did not know or has not replied in the agreed time, alert the class teacher or coordinator on a dashboard so a staff member phones the family.
  • On RFID or attendant app events, notify the parent of boarding and drop, and send route delay notices only after the transport in-charge approves them.
  • If a child expected at a drop point is not marked off, alert the transport in-charge and the bus attendant at once to resolve by phone.
  • Show daily absences, late arrivals and unresolved cases, and give counselors a weekly list of repeated absences to follow up personally.

Human checkpoint

A named staff member phones every family that did not know about an absence, and the transport in-charge handles every missed drop or unusual delay by phone. Absence patterns are reviewed by the counselor or coordinator and never trigger automatic action.

Schools stay within the attendance and travel-safety purposes the DPDP Rules allow; coaching institutes rely on recorded parental consent. Boarding logs are deleted after the term.

Attend and learnStandard3–4 weeks

Teacher absence and substitution planner

Leave recorded before a cutoff produces a proposed substitution plan from the timetable, matching free teachers by subject and sharing extra periods fairly. The vice-principal approves it, and substitutes get their periods and lesson notes before the first bell.

K-12 schools · Coaching & test-prep institutes

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Substitutions are worked out on paper before assembly by the one person who knows the timetable. The same willing teachers absorb most extra periods, lesson notes rarely reach the substitute, and in coaching an absent faculty member can leave a batch waiting with no class.

Trigger

A teacher records leave in the ERP or HR system, or submits a leave request through the staff form, before the daily cutoff.

How it runs

  • Read approved and pending leave for the day and list the periods or batch lectures that need cover.
  • Find teachers free in each period, preferring the same subject and class, and balance cover using each teacher's load for the week and term.
  • Show the proposed plan to the vice-principal or academic coordinator, with conflicts and unfilled periods highlighted.
  • On approval, notify each substitute with class, room and the absent teacher's lesson plan link, and update the display timetable.
  • In coaching, offer the coordinator a reschedule option for lectures that cannot be covered, and notify the batch once it is approved.
  • Report substitution load by teacher and term so leadership can see whether cover is shared fairly.

Human checkpoint

The vice-principal or academic coordinator approves every plan and can override any assignment. Leave approval stays with the principal or HR under the staff leave policy; the planner never approves or rejects leave.

Assess and reportAdvanced5–7 weeks

Test analytics and doubt routing to faculty

Each mock test produces a private topic and time analysis against the student's own history for the student, parent and mentor. Doubts sent as photos or text are tagged by subject and chapter and queued to the right faculty, with similar solved questions attached.

Coaching & test-prep institutes · EdTech & online learning

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Test results show marks and ranks but not which topics or habits cost marks. Doubts sent by photo in crowded groups wait days or reach the wrong teacher, and mentors notice a struggling student only after several poor tests.

Trigger

Results of a mock or practice test are published from the test platform or OMR scanner, or a student submits a doubt in the app, portal or doubt WhatsApp number.

How it runs

  • Import question-level responses and compute accuracy and time by subject, chapter and difficulty, compared with the student's previous tests.
  • Publish a private analysis to the student and, for minors, the parent, with practice sets from the institute's own question bank and no public rank lists.
  • Alert the student's mentor when scores drop sharply or tests are missed, with the analysis attached for a conversation.
  • Read submitted doubt photos or text, tag subject, chapter and question type, and attach similar solved questions from the institute's bank.
  • Queue each doubt to the right faculty or doubt solver with a response target; faculty may start from an AI-drafted hint that they edit before sending.
  • Report doubt volume, resolution time and recurring weak topics to the academic head for remedial classes.

Human checkpoint

Faculty answer every doubt and approve any drafted hint before it reaches a student. Mentors decide on counseling or extra classes, and any sign of stress or distress goes to the institute's counselor, never to an automated message.

Pay, renew and stay connectedStarter2–3 weeks

Respectful fee reminders, payment links and receipts

Fee payers receive courteous reminders before and after due dates with a UPI payment link, receipts arrive instantly, and installment, concession or refund requests go to the accounts office. Reminders never reach children, class groups or noticeboards.

K-12 schools · Colleges & universities · Coaching & test-prep institutes

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Accounts staff chase dues by phone, reminders sometimes reach the wrong parent or a class group, and children can be embarrassed when dues are raised in class. Installment and refund requests get lost between the front office and accounts, and receipts are issued by hand.

Trigger

A fee installment approaches or passes its due date in the ERP fee ledger, a payment succeeds or fails at the gateway, or a fee payer asks about fees.

How it runs

  • Read due dates, amounts and concessions from the ERP fee ledger and send an approved reminder to the registered fee payer a set number of days before the due date.
  • Include a payment link for UPI, cards and net banking, and post successful payments to the ledger with an instant receipt, or a GST invoice where the fee is taxable.
  • After the due date, send no more than the agreed number of courteous reminders, each with an option to request an installment plan or speak to accounts.
  • Route installment, concession, scholarship and refund requests to the accounts officer with the student's ledger summary and the applicable refund policy.
  • Give accounts a daily view of dues, promises to pay and failed payments, with no list shared with teachers or classes.

Human checkpoint

The accounts officer decides installment plans, concessions and refunds, and the principal or registrar approves reminder wording and frequency. Any step that affects a student's classes, exams or results is a management decision under the institution's policy and the law, never automated.
